# 0.6 scope and upstream comparison

The upstream reference is the local dsh-ops checkout `61ef553` (2026-10-27), with
current upstream documentation consulted for public integration contracts. This
adapter reuses its native worker; equal worker capability is reuse, not a claim
that Codex Ops independently outperforms dsh-ops.

| Direction | Delivered surface | Remaining boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Composable workflows | locate, diagnose, documents, incremental; executable JS helper and types; native command-to-diagnosis composition | Explicit helper, not Desktop dynamic tool registration. Commands keep native permissions. |
| Useful evidence | Test/build/compiler diagnostics, Git diff/status and MCP list summaries; raw references | Deterministic supported profiles; unfamiliar results retain general presentation behavior. |
| Incremental and grouped output | Explicit owner/root/range-bound baseline comparisons; shared frame budget | No assumption that prior model context survives; frame budget is soft for retrieval/media and irreducible text. |
| Native tasks | Ordered stages, files and bounded trees, status/cancel/resume/rollback, interruption recovery | Journals are not atomic transactions; metadata publication can still be denied by native Windows policy. |
| Isolation and installation | Chat/permission-bound MCP refs, runtime-bound auto refs, current-process version checks, read-only dashboard | Runtime identity is not chat identity; same-OS-user hostile clients are outside this boundary; no native Codex sidebar. |
| Evaluation | 20 distinct tasks, two repetitions, native/0.5/0.6; native independent oracle; retained failures | Equivalent injected skill/hook guidance, not actual per-trial hook invocation. No DSH efficiency claim without comparable model/harness conditions. |

Correctness, raw values, diagnostics, current permissions and CRAP ≤6 are release
requirements. Target reductions of 25% in calls and 20% in input tokens are measured
objectives, not assumptions or release claims. Record regressions and comparable
pair counts before interpreting medians. Cache input, noncache input and output are
reported separately. Prototype or aggregate byte savings are not token-cost savings.

Native Desktop integration consists of the supported local plugin surface plus an
explicit version-tested Code Mode bridge. OpenAI binaries and model traffic are not
modified. Unknown host versions forward unchanged; host updates require revalidation.
